These pages are for you if you change SCGSim itself: its code, its tests or
its documentation. They take you from the folder tree of `src/scgsim` down to
the contract of the folder you work in, then give the commands that check a
change before you open a pull request. To use SCGSim for a simulation, start
from [Install SCGSim](../start/install.qmd) instead.

## Set up a checkout {#set-up}

Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) and Git,
then:

```bash
git clone --branch develop https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim.git
cd scgsim
uv sync --locked --group dev
```

The `dev` group installs every optional extra with the test, quality and
OpenCASCADE tools, the same set the CI test jobs install. Native Palace and
AEDT are not part of it; no check below needs them.

## Read in this order {#reading-order}

1. [Code map](code-map.qmd): the folders of `src/scgsim`, which stage each
   one is, the order the work flows through them on the Palace and the AEDT
   route, and the import order CI checks. Every other page assumes it.
2. [Architecture](architecture.qmd): who owns which state, and the
   lifecycle of a Palace run and of an AEDT run.
3. [Ownership by area](ownership.qmd): what each area must not take over
   from another, and what stays outside SCGSim.
4. The contract page of the folder you change, in Reference:
   [GeometryPlan](../reference/specs/geometry-plan.qmd) for `geometry`,
   [Mesh quality](../reference/specs/mesh-quality.qmd) for `meshing`, the
   [Palace Electrostatic](../reference/specs/palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd) and
   [Palace Eigenmode](../reference/specs/palace-eigenmode.qmd) specifications
   for `palace`, the [AEDT runtime](../reference/specs/aedt-runtime.qmd) for
   `aedt`, and the [report model](../reference/specs/report-model.qmd) for
   results and reports. [Supported calculations](../reference/supported-calculations.qmd)
   and [Supported scope](../reference/supported-scope.qmd) say what a change
   must keep working.
5. The pages of the **Internals** section of this sidebar: the parts of a
   folder's design that its contract page leaves out.
6. For work in `geometry/sgb`, the
   [SGB design pages](../../zh-TW/docs/contribute/sgb-design/index.html)
   (in Traditional Chinese): why the builder plans before it writes, and each
   stage from the prisms to the files.

[Provenance](provenance.qmd), the [notebook contract](notebook-contract.qmd),
the [documentation map](documentation-map.qmd) and
[Scope and origin](goals-and-upstream.qmd) answer narrower questions; read
them when your change touches what they cover.

## Check a change {#check}

Run these from the root of the checkout. The first two are the `quality` and
`fast-tests` jobs of CI, with the same arguments:

```bash
uv run --locked --no-sync python scripts/check_quality.py
uv run --locked --no-sync python -m pytest tests -m 'not slow and not private_golden and not pdk' -rs --fail-on-skip
```

`check_quality.py` runs Ruff formatting and lint, the readable-style check,
Pyright and the import-layer contracts over every tracked Python file. The
test run fails on a skip, because the `dev` group installs everything the
tests need.

For a documentation change, also check the generated pages and render the
site (Quarto in the range `scripts/build_docs_site.py` names):

```bash
uv run --locked --no-sync python scripts/generate_code_map.py --check
uv run --locked --no-sync python scripts/generate_knowledge_reference.py --check
quarto render --no-execute
```

The render builds the English site into `_site/` and then the Chinese site
into `_site/zh-TW/`. No notebook cell and no solver runs.

## Rules and delivery {#rules}

- [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim/blob/develop/AGENTS.md):
  what the repository owns, how work is delivered, and how a pull request is
  reviewed.
- [`CODE_STYLE.md`](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim/blob/develop/CODE_STYLE.md):
  how SCGSim's Python is written.
- [`DOCS_STYLE.md`](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim/blob/develop/DOCS_STYLE.md):
  how the documentation is written, which source owns which page, and the
  Chinese terms.
- [`MAINTAINING.md`](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim/blob/develop/MAINTAINING.md):
  the maintainer guide: what each CI job checks, the documentation build and
  the generated pages.

A change goes to `develop` through a pull request whose body starts with the
line `Issue:` and the Issue it answers, as the
[pull request template](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim/blob/develop/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md)
shows.
